newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner posts profit for quarter, loss for year.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner posts profit for quarter, loss for year.

text.p: Time Warner Inc. said Tuesday that its profits soared 79 percent in the fourth quarter, helped by its acquisition of Turner Broadcasting System Inc., although its loss for all of 1996 was greater than a year earlier.
The huge communications conglomerate said its net income jumped to $59 million in the three months ended Dec. 31, although that translated to a loss of 3 cents a share.
The latest earnings compared with a year-ago profit of $33 million, or 1 cent a share.
The per-share figures were based on 558.7 million shares outstanding in the fourth quarter of 1996, compared with 387.5 million in the 1995 quarter.
For the full year, Time Warner said it lost $191 million, or $1.04 a share, which was 15 percent worse than its loss of $166 million, or 57 cents a share, in 1995.
Those per-share amounts were based on 431.2 million shares outstanding in 1996 and 383.8 million in 1995.
The 1996 results included an extraordinary loss of $35 million on the retirement of debt, compared with an extraordinary loss of $42 million on the retirement of debt in 1995.
The company said its revenues in the latest quarter grew 31 percent to $6.7 billion from $5.1 billion. For the full year revenues expanded 18 percent to $20.9 billion from $17.7 billion.
The company noted that all the earnings figures reflect the businesses of Turner Broadcasting, which Time Warner acquired in October 1996.
Time Warner said its fourth-quarter earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, often referred to as cash flow, rose 34 percent to a record $1.4 billion from $1.0 billion.
For the full year, cash flow expanded 30 percent to a record $4.3 billion from $3.3 billion.
"I am very pleased with our 34 percent growth, which led to record EBITDA in the quarter," Time Warner Chairman Gerald M. Levin said in a statement.

The company said its cash flow improved significantly at all its major businesses in the quarter. It said Home Box Office grew by 25 percent, Time Inc. by 14 percent and Time Warner Cable by 32 percent.
"The business units of Time Warner continue to lead their industries," Levin said.

Time Warner said the performance of the Turner Networks remained outstanding. TNT, CNN and the TBS Superstation now reach over 70 million households each and the Cartoon Network is in 40 million homes, the company said.

It said its results were also helped by three big movie hits last year. It said "Twister," "Eraser" and "A Time To Kill" each pulled in more than $100 million at the box office, which it said was a first in movie history.
The company also said that Warner Bros. television continued to lead the ratings with the hit shows "ER" and "Friends," as well as one of the season's new hits, "Suddenly Susan."
Time Warner's stock gained 62.5 cents to $40.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was among the most-active issues.
